What we carry

Four reasons to make the drive.

Tap any one to see what's behind it.

$8.99* a yard

Quality quilting cotton off the bolt, cut at the counter, priced so a whole quilt is still worth starting. Bring the pattern in and we'll help you get the yardage right the first time.

*Specialty fabrics included, per the shop's window sign.

Rulers, rotary blades, thread, needles, marking tools — plus the pattern shelf, so you can walk out with the fabric and the instructions in the same bag.

If you've seen a block you like and can't name it, bring a photo. Naming blocks is half of what happens at this counter.

Classes run from a first quilt through work that takes a while — whether you're learning to piece your first block or chasing something more ambitious, there's a seat for it.

Call the shop for what's on the calendar right now; class sizes are small on purpose.

Ask what's running

Piecing a top is one job; quilting it is another. Bring the finished top in and it gets quilted here — no shipping it off, no wondering where it went.

Call with the size of your top and what you'd like done to it, and you'll get a straight answer on cost and timing.

The shop

“I truly believe sewing soothes the soul.”

Lorna has run Front Porch Quilts on Main Street since the shop opened — wife, mother, grandmother, and a quilter first.

She learned to sew in 4-H in the third grade and has had a passion for it ever since. For years it was garment sewing. Then one day she decided to try her hand at making a quilt, gave up garments entirely, and never looked back.

The shop sits in the foothills, in a town whose mantra is “Below the Snow and Above the Clouds.” Her hope for anyone who walks through the door is a simple one: to leave inspired — whether that's quilting, garment sewing or craft sewing.

Getting here

Stop in, or call ahead.

  1. Bring what you're working on

    A pattern, a photo of a block, a finished top for longarm — anything you want a second pair of eyes on.

  2. Talk it through at the counter

    Yardage, colour, what to do next. This is the part that doesn't happen online.

  3. Leave with the fabric and a plan

    Cut to your numbers, with the pattern and notions to match.
